title: Trustworthy Process Monitor — run report
subtitle: Data-reliability report for an undocumented tabular data stream
overview_dataset: The run processed {rows} rows and {cols} columns from {source} ({format}). {n_signals} columns were treated as signals and {n_excluded} were excluded from detection (labels, identifiers, constants, derived duplicates). The data was split into {groups} groups ({method}) and {batches} batches.
overview_dataset_missing: The ingest stage did not produce a schema in this run, so the dataset summary is not available.
overview_quality: {n_checks} baseline and rule checks ran: {n_pass} passed, {n_warn} warned, {n_fail} failed. {n_untrusted} of {n_batches} batches could not be trusted.
overview_detect: {n_flags} events were flagged in {n_groups_flagged} groups; {n_patterns} recurring fault patterns were found.
overview_diag: {n_diag} root-cause diagnoses were produced (mean confidence {mean_conf}); the critique step weakened {n_weak} and rejected {n_rej} of them.
overview_human: {n_human} human decisions were recorded and fed back into the run.
overview_egress: {n_external} external model calls were made under the '{profile}' profile; {n_blocked} were blocked by the egress guard. Raw rows never left the operator environment.
overview_egress_none: No external model calls were made: the '{profile}' profile keeps every model call inside the operator environment.
overview_chain: The decision log holds {n} hash-chained entries.
s1_intro: Every role below is inferred from the data itself. Column headers, when present, are treated as weak evidence only (blind mode). A lower-confidence inference with visible evidence is preferred over an asserted label.
s1_no_signals: The profile stage produced no signal catalog in this run.
unc_instrument: The instrument type is a hypothesis ({conf}) generated from general domain knowledge, not a fact.
unc_assumed: An inference about this signal is marked '{status}'.
unc_none: No specific uncertainty recorded beyond the confidence value.
s2_intro: Baseline checks (completeness, validity, consistency, timeliness) run on every batch before any drift or fault reasoning. Rule checks are compiled from plain-language rules and trace back to their rule ID.
s2_trust_note: When the trust score of a batch falls below {threshold}, the report states that the data itself cannot be trusted and downstream flags for that batch carry lower confidence.
s2_no_untrusted: All batches passed the trust threshold.
s2_no_rules: No plain-language rules were supplied in this run. Rules can be added from the UI or with --rules FILE.
s2_no_checks: The quality stage produced no checks in this run.
dq_verdict_untrusted: This data cannot be trusted as a whole: {n_bad} of {n_batches} batches ({pct} of the rows) failed the trust check{because}.
dq_verdict_partly: Parts of this data cannot be trusted: {n_bad} of {n_batches} batches ({pct} of the rows) failed the trust check{because}.
dq_verdict_usable: This data is usable, but not clean: every batch passed the trust check, yet {n_fail} checks failed and {n_warn} warned; the affected rows and signals are set aside.
dq_verdict_clean: This data passed the baseline checks: every batch can be trusted.
dq_not_testable: {n} checks could not be run ({cats}): the data lacks what they need, for example a time column. They count as neither passed nor failed.
s3_intro: Every row was scored out-of-fold by an ensemble of detectors that never saw its own group during fitting. The timelines show the ensemble score per group (max per bucket); the horizontal line is the alert threshold and shaded areas are flagged rows. Every flag names the signals responsible.
s3_no_scores: No score timeline is available in this run (scores.parquet missing).
s3_no_flags: No events were flagged in this run.
s3_evaluation_note: Metrics come from label-like columns that were auto-detected and excluded from detection; they are used for evaluation only.
s4_intro: Each diagnosis names a fault type, ranks the contributing signals with a plain-language reason, shows the propagation chain, gives a step-by-step explanation for a non-expert, states its confidence and what remains uncertain, and includes the result of the critique step that challenged it.
s4_no_diag: No diagnoses were produced in this run.
s5_intro: Every inference, flag, diagnosis, rule and pattern can be accepted, questioned, overridden or dismissed by a named operator, engineer or reviewer. Decisions are logged with the state before and after and feed back into later stages.
s5_no_human: No human decisions were recorded in this run. Open the run in the UI to accept, question or override any output.
s6_intro: Every system decision (inference, check, flag, diagnosis, egress, stage) and every human decision is appended to a SQLite log whose entries are SHA-256 hash-chained. Tampering with any entry breaks the chain.
chain_ok: Hash chain verified: {n} entries, no tampering detected.
chain_bad: Hash chain BROKEN at entry {seq} ({n} entries verified before the break).
s6_appendix_note: Showing the first {shown} of {total} entries. The complete log is exported as decision_log.jsonl.
s7_intro: The pipeline is schema-agnostic by construction: nothing in it knows what a reactor or an invoice is. The same stages run unchanged on sensor streams, manually entered business records and log-derived tables; only the reader and the structural role vocabulary adapt.
s7_generic: Stages that are identical for every domain: ingestion to aliased columns (S01…Snn), structural role inference from fingerprints, grouping and batching, baseline-regime selection, out-of-fold anomaly scoring with per-signal attribution, change-point detection, pattern clustering, rule compilation into the same closed check vocabulary, diagnosis assembly and critique, decision log, egress guard.
s7_adapters: What changes per domain: the file reader (CSV / whitespace .dat / Parquet / Excel / JSON), the weight given to categorical and text columns, and the vocabulary of instrument hypotheses (which is a hypothesis layer only).
s7_example: A drifting sensor and a corrupted batch of records flow through the same pipeline: both appear as a group of rows whose fingerprint and correlation structure move away from the baseline, both are attributed to specific columns, and both are diagnosed as 'sensor/data' (one column breaks its relations) or 'process' (several related columns move together).
s7_link: Full walkthrough: docs/ADAPTABILITY.md. Domain likelihood measured for this dataset:
s8_intro: This record states what left the operator environment, to which model, and why. Raw rows are never sent anywhere; external models receive only derived artifacts that passed the egress guard.
s8_stays_items: raw rows, dataset.parquet, scores.parquet, every prompt sent to the local model, the decision log, all reports
s8_leaves: May leave (only under a profile that allows external calls, and only after passing the guard)
s8_leaves_items: signal catalog aggregates (count, mean, std, quantiles), relation summaries (r, lag), check / flag / diagnosis statements with signal aliases, plain-language rule text
s8_guard_items: aggregates need ≥ {min_n} samples; no series longer than {max_series} points; at most {max_vals} numeric values per payload; payload ≤ {max_bytes} bytes; no categorical / free-text values; no row-like structures; in strict mode column names are replaced by aliases
s8_no_ledger: No model calls were recorded in this run.
s8_swap_text: Set TPM_PROFILE (no-egress | hybrid | eu-hosted) or edit config/settings.yaml. local_llm.model selects the Ollama model; external_llm.base_url points the external route at an EU-hosted endpoint. No code changes are needed.
statement_no_egress: Under the '{profile}' profile no data of any kind left the operator environment. All {n_local} model calls were served by the local model '{local_model}' through Ollama on this machine.
statement_external: Under the '{profile}' profile {n_external} calls were sent to '{external_model}' ({provider}); each carried only derived artifacts that passed the egress guard ({bytes} bytes in total). {n_blocked} payloads were blocked and served locally instead. {n_local} calls were served by the local model '{local_model}'. Raw rows never left the machine.
eval_intro: Label-like columns were auto-detected and excluded from detection. They are read only here, after detection, to measure how well the unsupervised pipeline did.
eval_no: No label-like columns were found, so no evaluation metrics are available. This is the expected situation for assessment data.
assessor_intro: The assessor judges how fit the dataset is for unsupervised monitoring and what more data would buy, leading with ML fitness and coverage. Recommendations are advice only; nothing is applied without approval.
assessor_no: The assessor stage produced no result in this run.
llm_label: Written by a language model ({source}) from derived artifacts only (no raw rows). It is a reading aid, not evidence: every finding in this report is computed by code and backed by evidence IDs.
llm_truncated: the reply was cut by the length limit; only complete sentences are shown
llm_pending: The model-written summary was still being written when this page was rendered. The report below is complete without it; reload the page in about a minute to see the summary.
capped_flags: Showing the {shown} most severe of {total} flags. The complete list is in flags.jsonl of the run workspace and in the Monitor view; the counts below cover all flags.
capped_diagnoses: Showing the {shown} diagnoses with the most severe flags, of {total}. The complete list is in diagnoses.jsonl of the run workspace and in the Diagnoses view.
capped_untrusted: Showing the {shown} batches with the lowest trust score, of {total} untrusted batches.
llm_not_used: No model-written summary: the language model was not available or was disabled for this report. All content above is template-generated from the artifacts.
email_body: The Trustworthy Process Monitor report for run {run_id} is attached ({lang}). Source: {source}. Profile: {profile}.
susp_intro: Rows where a reading stands out from its neighbours, from its own history or from an allowed range. Each row is listed once, strongest first, whichever check found it.
susp_wording_default: Glitch or manipulation: the data alone can't tell.
susp_regime: {n_points} isolated stretches and {n_sustained} sustained stretches were found; isolated readings make up {share} of the suspicious rows.
susp_point_dominated: Most of what stands out in this run is isolated readings rather than sustained events.
susp_capped: Showing the {shown} strongest of {total} suspicious rows.
susp_point_flags: Isolated readings flagged by the monitor ({n})
susp_none_listed: No individual rows are listed for this run.
overview_suspicious: {n} suspicious rows were listed; whether they are glitches or manipulation cannot be told from the data alone.
pdf_capped_rows: Showing {shown} of {total}; the complete list is in the run workspace and in the HTML report.
pdf_no_raw: Generated on this machine from derived artifacts only. The document contains no raw rows.
pdf_timeline_caption: Line: ensemble score (highest value per bucket). Dashed line: alert threshold. Shaded: flagged rows.
pdf_timelines_shown: {shown} of {total} groups are drawn: those with the most flags.
pdf_trust_all: Trust verdicts: {trusted} of {total} batches trusted; lowest trust score {low}.
px_assessor: Would more or less data help?
px_next: What remains uncertain and next steps
px_trust_by_block: Lowest trust score per block of batches
px_sensor_vs_process: Sensor or data faults versus process faults
px_sensor_vs_process_text: {n_sensor} flagged events point at a single sensor or at the data itself, {n_process} at the process, and {n_other} are mixed or unknown. A lone signal that breaks away from its partners is treated as a sensor or data problem; several related signals moving together as a process fault.
px_groups_over: {n_over} of {n_groups} groups crossed the alert threshold.
px_nothing_left: Nothing left the machine: no payload was sent to an external model.
px_left_text: {n_external} calls carried derived artifacts only ({bytes} bytes) to {model}; {n_blocked} payloads were blocked by the egress guard.
px_shortened: Text shortened to fit the slide; the full wording is in the report.
px_notes_none: This slide is built from run totals; no single evidence id applies.
px_next_review: Review the {n} diagnoses in the app and accept, question or override them.
px_next_untrusted: Repair the data path of the {n} untrusted batches before relying on their flags.
px_next_suspicious: Decide with the process owner whether the suspicious rows are glitches or manipulation.
px_next_baseline: Confirm the baseline regime or set a reference period: no normal data was provided, so "normal" is an estimate.

px_unc_no_labels: No labels were available, so detection quality could not be measured in this run.

footer: Trustworthy Process Monitor — every claim links to evidence IDs (EV-…) recorded in the run workspace. Print this page to PDF for a shareable copy.
baseline_why: Why this baseline, and what breaks if it is wrong
baseline_why_text: The app tried several ways to find 'normal' in the data and kept '{chosen}' (it describes {fraction} of the sampled rows). The runner-up was '{runner}', {margin} lower on the combined score below.
baseline_breaks: What breaks if the baseline is wrong: faulty rows inside it look normal, so similar faults are missed; a normal operating mode missing from it is reported as unusual. Name a known-normal period (Data quality page or --opt reference_period=...) to replace the guess.
eval_headline: of the rows inside events, {precision} were really abnormal (precision); {recall} of the abnormal rows were found (recall). False alarms: {false_alarm} of {n_normal} normal groups; detected: {detection} of {n_abnormal} abnormal groups.
eval_conf_note: Confidence is a heuristic score (detector agreement, strength and length of the event, baseline confidence). This table shows how often it was right on this labelled data; labels are never used for detection.
spread_headline: No single signal dominates: about {n} signals are needed to explain half of the change (the strongest carries {top}).
heatmap_intro: Correlation between the {n} most connected signals, measured on normal-looking rows.
lag_line: {lead} moves first; {follow} follows about {lag} samples later (correlation {r}).
trends_intro: {n} events were classified as gradual drift. For the strongest drifts (then the longest other events) the plot shows the leading signal through the event: the shaded band is its normal range (median +- 3 robust spreads on the normal rows), red dots are readings outside it.
trend_stats: trend over the event: Kendall's tau {tau}, {sig} at the 1 % level; {outside} of the readings outside the normal band
trends_none: No drift or long event to plot.
